question: What is going wrong with my payments?
dataset: sample data: 6,000 made-up payments for a made-up shop, with a UPI problem planted to show what the output looks like. It is not a real business

findings.title: Failed rate varies by method: upi 9.6% versus card 2.8%
findings.headline: Failed rate differs by method: upi is highest at 9.6%, card is lowest at 2.8% (238% apart).
reasoning: Based on 3,315 and 1,513 rows; the gap is about 10.1 standard errors, well beyond chance.
why: Based on 3,315 upi rows and 1,513 card rows.
Random sampling alone would almost never produce a gap this large.
findings.confidence_note: Far larger than random ups and downs can explain.
findings.sql: SELECT "method" AS grp, COUNT((CASE WHEN "status" IS NULL OR TRIM("status") = '' THEN NULL WHEN LOWER(TRIM("status")) = 'failed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)) AS n, AVG((CASE WHEN "status" IS NULL OR TRIM("status") = '' THEN NULL WHEN LOWER(TRIM("status")) = 'failed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)) AS mean, SUM((CASE WHEN "status" IS NULL OR TRIM("status") = '' THEN NULL WHEN LOWER(TRIM("status")) = 'failed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)*(CASE WHEN "status" IS NULL OR TRIM("status") = '' THEN NULL WHEN LOWER(TRIM("status")) = 'failed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)) AS sq, COUNT(CASE WHEN (CASE WHEN "status" IS NULL OR TRIM("status") = '' THEN NULL WHEN LOWER(TRIM("status")) = 'failed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN 1 END) AS npos, AVG(CASE WHEN (CASE WHEN "status" IS NULL OR TRIM("status") = '' THEN NULL WHEN LOWER(TRIM("status")) = 'failed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN ln((CASE WHEN "status" IS NULL OR TRIM("status") = '' THEN NULL WHEN LOWER(TRIM("status")) = 'failed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)) END) AS lmean, SUM(CASE WHEN (CASE WHEN "status" IS NULL OR TRIM("status") = '' THEN NULL WHEN LOWER(TRIM("status")) = 'failed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN ln((CASE WHEN "status" IS NULL OR TRIM("status") = '' THEN NULL WHEN LOWER(TRIM("status")) = 'failed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END))*ln((CASE WHEN "status" IS NULL OR TRIM("status") = '' THEN NULL WHEN LOWER(TRIM("status")) = 'failed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)) END) AS lsq FROM "payments" WHERE (CASE WHEN "status" IS NULL OR TRIM("status") = '' THEN NULL WHEN LOWER(TRIM("status")) = 'failed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) IS NOT NULL AND "method" IS NOT NULL GROUP BY grp HAVING COUNT((CASE WHEN "status" IS NULL OR TRIM("status") = '' THEN NULL WHEN LOWER(TRIM("status")) = 'failed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)) >= 10
followups: Why is failed rate highest for method upi?

findings.title: Failed rate rose from 5.8% to 9.3% starting September 2026, almost all of it in method upi (7.4% to 14.4%)
findings.so_what: That is about 66 more failed rows than the earlier rate would have given, out of 1,904.
findings.headline: The failed rate rose from 5.8% to 9.3% starting September 2026, almost all of it in method upi (7.4% to 14.4%).
reasoning: Before: 238 of 4,096 rows (5.8%). After: 177 of 1,904 rows (9.3%).
The best split point was searched among 9 possible ones, and the result still stands far beyond chance.
why: A change this large and this lasting is very unlikely from random variation.
findings.confidence_note: Probably real, but close to the edge of what chance can explain.
findings.sql: SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', "created_at") AS period, COUNT((CASE WHEN "status" IS NULL OR TRIM("status") = '' THEN NULL WHEN LOWER(TRIM("status")) = 'failed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)) AS n, SUM((CASE WHEN "status" IS NULL OR TRIM("status") = '' THEN NULL WHEN LOWER(TRIM("status")) = 'failed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)) AS events FROM "payments" WHERE "created_at" IS NOT NULL AND (CASE WHEN "status" IS NULL OR TRIM("status") = '' THEN NULL WHEN LOWER(TRIM("status")) = 'failed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) IS NOT NULL GROUP BY period ORDER BY period
